summary: The customer wants to know whether optical spectroscopy can monitor composition changes in-line during hot melt extrusion of an active pharmaceutical ingredient, and requires an evaluation plan and probe selection criteria.

facts_stated.text: The application is a hot polymer extrusion process incorporating an active pharmaceutical ingredient.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: hot polymer extrusion process that incorporates an active pharmaceutical ingredient

facts_stated.text: The material is being processed as a melt.
The process interface operates at elevated temperature.
The process interface may experience material accumulation.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: may be exposed to material build up

targets.purpose: detect composition changes while the melt is being processed

process.enquiry_quote: may be exposed to material build up

unknowns: Identity and formulation of the polymer matrix and active pharmaceutical ingredient (API)
Target concentration range, required detection limit, and measurement precision
Specific process operating temperature and pressure ranges at the probe interface
Optical characteristics of the polymer melt (e.g., clear, turbid, scattering, or absorbing)
Physical interface specifications (extruder barrel/die port dimensions, thread type, mechanical clearances)
Required measurement response time or sampling frequency
Details on the offline assay used as a reference method
Fouling behavior, material residence time at the optical window, and maintenance or cleaning capabilities
